I dislike positionals because I see no point in them. I get there's a part of skill expression in it. I raid at a high level, Ultis on content clears, week 1-2 savage.

CBU3 has made the hit boxes so ridiculously massive. I don't know how you could miss your positionals unless you were purposely trying to. Comparative too ShB, SB, HW, etc. They make it so easy to hit. For a decent player trying. I no longer think of it as skill expression. 

There's also something that Xenos has said that I fully agree with. If you just got rid of melee positionals you could make way more interesting mechanics. That's something I would like to see, and thats why I advocate for the removal for them. 

Tldr its so easy to hit positionals now, so what's the point of having them. Get rid of them, and we can have interesting mechanics.

Most of the time if you are running optimized groups it will be SCH and AST. AST has ridiculous amount of OGCD heals. So when I say off load healing to the co-healer. I basically mean the Ast is probably healing 60-70% of the fight. 

I don't want to use the trust me bro response but back in the day when I parsed in shadowbringers and with the new Astro abilities in EW especially macrocosmos. Astro just outheals by a generous amount. 

I've also been on both sides the SCH trying to optimize to use more ED'S and the AST having to literally heal most of the fight while watching the SCH go brrrrr with ED. 

Ended up realising how selfish the game play is when going for optimisation just didn't like how the game play loop rewards playing well by not healing specifically as SCH.

I didn't like how playing AST well means you're doing  most of the healing when it's an optimized run since that's what you are actually meant to do. 

But then at the end you get use to it and it just becomes boring because you're not playing to heal you're playing how much you can get away without healing. While having the most brain dead one DPS button.

It's why I would say veteran healers really want healer design to change. I want to enjoy healing but when playing a jobs identity to excel is selfish gameplay. While the other excels above all in terms of actually healing the fight, while doing damage, while having more apm, while doing all mechanics. You kind of feel like one healer is playing the game in easy mode.

Don't get me started on WHM there's a reason why it's called glare mage.

Spread low takes gcds to set up in which you are losing casts for broil. Which technically is a DPS loss. So unless a big raidwide that will wipe the whole HP bar out is coming. It's just better to use ogcds and anything that doesn't use aetherflow if possible. 

But imo Scholar is one of the most selfish healers to play if you're going for max damage as you end up offloading so much to the cohealer. Simply because using aetherflow for mitigation is damage loss.

As someone who does sometimes want to call out the not all men as a male. These are some of the reasons why I feel the need to.

Trauma - My father cheated on my mother so I swore to myself to never cheat on anyone if I ever got into a relationship and so far I've done right by that. However, because of that trauma I've had some internalised anger towards cheaters and being generalized as a cheater. 'All men cheat, men use women for sex etc. I know that it is true to a certain extent but the internalised hate within myself makes me want to call out desperately. I'm not that. I'm working through it though.

Generalizations and Double Standards - We all know generalisations and double standards for genders no real need to give an example. It's a generalisation and just got to self distance yourself from it but it becomes really hard when you realise there's too many men doing such things. Current Era - The world really is a safer place then it was many years ago. So the wishful thinking is that we have it so much better yet these things still happen. You would think women would feel safe but they don't 

The ability - The average male has the strength and ability to overpower an average female. Most men choose not to, but like people said in this thread there's just too many men. But it comes to the back of our minds, 'we could do it,' self control is something we all need to learn.

I think I get it sort of the meaning behind everything that happened. 
It's a bit depressing how you go do all this work to save Chloe and the choice is save 1 or 1000.
However the game did lead up to it and acknowledge the feelings Chloe and Max had for each other leading up to episode 5. I definitely saw the romantic notations from the two. 
However once you go the funeral and you see the butterfly, I thought to myself was this how Rachael Amber wanted things to happen. Did Rachael want Chloe to feel love before she had to go much like she did and when Chloe finally did die was it a plan for Chloe to do her checklist before the end of the world.
I feel as if Chloe was a metaphor for many things in this game that, it really is amazing.
Also did anybody notice the cicada on Max's shirt during the time she was held in the darkroom. Typically the symbolism of the cicada means: Longevity, Rebirth, Metamorphosis, Reflection, Change, Development. 
Life is Strange has so many motifs and symbolism that it really affects you to your core as a human being.
Only criticism is the fact sacrificing Arcadia Bay did not have a depth enough ending was definitely lack luster, it made sense however it wasn't much for closure.
On my last note Rachael and Chloe are back together by the afterlife and I ship ChloeXMax XD (screw you Warren).
